title: SmartOClock: Workload- and Risk-Aware Overclocking in the Cloud
problem: Overclocking server components in cloud environments improves performance and lowers costs, but significantly degrades component lifetime, increases power draw, and causes power capping events that diminish performance benefits. Cloud systems lack effective management mechanisms to balance these trade-offs across heterogeneous workloads and servers.
motivation: Cloud providers need to maximize performance and minimize costs from overclocking while managing hardware degradation and power constraints to optimize overall system efficiency.
method: SmartOClock manages overclocking (running server hardware faster than rated speed) across a cloud data center by analyzing real workload patterns to predict how much extra power each server will need if overclocked. Based on these power predictions and each server's hardware characteristics, the system calculates a safe overclocking power budget for each server. Each server then enforces its own power limit locally, without requiring a central controller to monitor compliance.
key_novelty: SmartOClock predicts how much power different workloads need when overclocked, then distributes power budgets to individual servers that enforce their own limits instead of using a central controller.
contributions: First distributed overclocking management platform specifically designed for cloud environments
Workload-aware power prediction and heterogeneous budget distribution mechanism
Decentralized per-server budget enforcement avoiding centralized coordination
Production Azure deployment demonstrating 9% tail latency reduction and 30% cost savings

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 10% energy consumption reduction, 30% application cost reduction
metrics.other: 95% reduction in power capping events, 62% increase in overclocking success rate

baselines: standard cloud operation without overclocking management
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations; evaluation is limited to 36-server deployment with simulation analysis using production traces.
